Where should the line be drawn?

Reject when the predicted default risk is at or above the cut-off. The payoff table puts the break-even at interest ÷ (1 + interest), which is 1 in 6 at 20 %. The coloured curve is the model picked above; grey curves are the rest. These curves use the test set in hindsight, while the tuned marker was chosen on training folds only.

Step 5 · the verdict

Recommendation to QuickLoan leadership

To: QuickLoan leadership · From: Risk team · Re: Which default model to deploy

Deploy the Stacking ensemble and reject any applicant whose default risk is 14 % or higher.

Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost and Logistic Regression each give a default probability; a logistic-regression manager weighs them. On 1,500 held-out applications it saves AED 6.01 M compared with approving everyone, about AED 4,000 per application and 49 % of the AED 12.27 M a perfect model could save.

Same 1,500 test loansMoney savedDefaulters caughtAccuracy
Approve everyone (naive policy)AED 00 of 18887.5 %
Best single model, 50 % rule (Decision Tree)AED 3.93 M52 (27.7 %)89.5 %
Brief's champion, 50 % rule (Gradient Boosting)AED 4.77 M63 (33.5 %)89.6 %
Stacking, 14 % cut-off (recommended)AED 6.01 M98 (52.1 %)86.0 %
  • Why Stacking. It saves the most money on the test set and the most on average across 10 cross-validation folds under both cut-off rules, and its probabilities are the best calibrated (lowest log-loss). Gradient Boosting at a 16 % cut-off is the closest runner-up.
  • Lower accuracy, on purpose. Accuracy falls from 89.5 % to 86.0 % because we turn away 120 good borrowers (each costs about 20 % of a loan in lost interest) to stop 98 defaulters (each saves 100 %).
  • Less interpretability. Permutation importance shows sensible drivers (debt-to-income, past defaults, income). Keep the logistic-regression scorecard as a challenger model and as the source of reason codes for rejected applicants.
  • Before go-live. Re-tune the cut-off whenever the interest rate changes, monitor caught / wrongly rejected / money saved every month, and validate on fresh applications, including a fairness check across home-ownership groups.

Data: loans.csv (6,000 applicants, 12.6 % defaulters). Stratified 75 / 25 split, random_state = 1 (the same split as app.py). Money saved = loans of caught defaulters − interest × loans of wrongly rejected borrowers, against approving everyone. Tuned cut-offs come from 5-fold out-of-fold predictions on the training set at each interest rate; the test set is only scored.
